newsitem.title: USA: Mont. Colstrip 330 MW unit start delayed for 1 wk.
newsitem.headline: Mont. Colstrip 330 MW unit start delayed for 1 wk.

text.p: Work to repair a cooling tower at the 330 megawatt (MW) unit 1 at the Colstrip coal-fired power plant will take about a week longer than expected, a spokesman for Montana Power Co. said Friday.
The unit has been out of service since early last week.
Colstrip's other units, another at 330 MW and two at 700 MW were operating normally, the spokesman said.
Montana Power operates the Colstrip plant, located near Billings, Mont., and is responsible for the sale of 30 percent of unit 4's output under long-term contracts.

Equity owners include Puget Sound Power and Light Co, Washington Water Power Co, Portland General Electric Co, Pacific Power and Light, and a consortium of GE Credit, Shell Oil Co and a lease-back firm.
